proof.convention: rho(sigma_i): x_i→x_i x_(i+1) x_i^-1, x_(i+1)→x_i, others fixed; multiply automorphisms by composition, rho(uv)=rho(u)∘rho(v).
proof.variables: r=m−1; a=x_1…x_r; y_j=x_(r+j) for j=1,…,r; b=y_1…y_r; z=x_(2m−1); P=x_1…x_m=a y_1; Q=b z; c=b z b^-1=Q z Q^-1.
proof.A_action: rho(A_m)(x_j)=P x_(m+j) P^-1 for 1≤j≤r, and rho(A_m)(x_(r+j))=x_j for 1≤j≤m. The formulas follow by substitution in the increasing list of descending rows, or induction on the number of rows.
proof.T_action: rho(T_m) conjugates x_1,…,x_m by P and fixes x_(m+1),…,x_(2m−1). This follows by m substitutions of rho(sigma_1…sigma_(m−1)): x_j↦x_1 x_(j+1) x_1^-1 for j<m and x_m↦x_1.
proof.B_action: rho(B_m)(y_1)=c, and rho(B_m)(x_(m+j))=y_j for 1≤j≤r; the first r free generators are fixed. These follow immediately through the descending generator list.
proof.D_action: Putting D_m=B_m T_m^-1 A_m gives rho(D_m)(x_j)=a c y_j c^-1 a^-1; rho(D_m)(y_j)=c^-1 a^-1 x_j a c for 1≤j≤r; and rho(D_m)(z)=c^-1 a^-1 c a c.
proof.W_r_action: rho(W_r)(x_j)=a b^-1 y_j b a^-1; rho(W_r)(y_j)=x_j for 1≤j≤r; rho(W_r)(z)=z. These follow by applying the equal-block swap C_r to the inverse first-block full twist.
proof.q_action: rho(q_m) fixes x_1,…,x_r and conjugates y_1,…,y_r,z by Q. In particular rho(q_m)(z)=c. Since rho(W_r)(Q)=a z, rho(q_m W_r q_m^-1) has exactly the three D_m formulas above.
proof.discharge: The automorphisms agree on every free generator. Faithfulness of the Artin representation therefore gives the stated group identity. This uses thm-the-artin-representation-is-faithful and its current recursive prerequisites if turned into a local item; it does not invoke a closure-isotopy-to-Markov implication.

ordinary_move_sequence: Write W_m=A_m sigma_(2m−1) B_m T_m^-1. Cyclic conjugation changes this to (B_m T_m^-1 A_m) sigma_(2m−1).
One positive ordinary destabilization removes the last generator sigma_(2m−1), giving D_m in B_(2m−1).
Conjugate by q_m^-1 to obtain W_(m−1) with one unused extra strand.

After the conjugation, W_(m−1) occupies the first 2m−2 strands and the last strand is unused. Put delta=sigma_1…sigma_(2m−2). The elementary braid identity delta sigma_i delta^-1=sigma_(i+1) for i≤2m−3 (apply the braid relation once and far-commute the remaining letters) moves this unused strand to the left and places the active W_(m−1) on the rightmost 2m−2 strands. Thus its next destabilization is again an ordinary rightmost destabilization. Repeat, carrying previously unused strands on the left. These unused strands are trivial and do not meet an external box.

Base m=1 gives W_1=sigma_1, which destabilizes to the identity in B_1. The induction ends at the identity m-braid after exactly m ordinary destabilizations. Reflection inverts all crossing signs and yields the negative version.
